extracted.intended_audience: public information officers and communications staff at NIH and its Institutes/Centers (ICs)
extracted.subtask_description: Style and usage rules for NIH web content, fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, and other promotional/press materials, with specific coordination and acknowledgement requirements for press releases. Emphasizes AP style as primary authority with supplemental HHS and NIH-specific guidance (person-first, destigmatizing language, accessibility, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Intended content types
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to web content, fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, and other promotional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guide is for NIH external-facing communications and promotional materials rather than scientific publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary style authority
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH primarily follows the Associated Press (AP) Stylebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where AP does not provide guidance, follow the HHS Style Guide. Use AP conventions for grammar, punctuation, and numerals unless NIH/HHS provide an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate government-related terms and conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP and HHS conventions for government names, agency terminology, capitalization, and titles; use official Institute/Center names when acknowledging funding or partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical language and person-first language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use medical language that prioritizes person-first constructions and avoids defining people by conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'person with diabetes' rather than 'diabetic' unless context/repeated usage requires otherwise; apply consistent, respectful terminology across materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destigmatizing language for conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use destigmatizing language when discussing conditions such as autism, obesity, disabilities, and substance use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pejorative or blaming phrasing; follow NIH examples/best practices for condition-specific terminology to reduce stigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age, race, and national origin terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use inclusive, accurate, and up-to-date terminology when describing age, race, and national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP/HHS/NIH recommendations for preferred terms and capitalization; be sensitive and specific where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar, punctuation, and numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow AP style rules for grammar, punctuation, and use of numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP conventions (e.g., number treatment, punctuation rules) unless NIH/HHS specify deviations for clarity or consistency in health communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt consistent structure and formatting for NIH communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply NIH formatting conventions for headers, bylines, datelines, contact/boilerplate blocks, and placement of acknowledgments/disclaimers (e.g., disclaimer may appear in footer or early in the release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomedical definitions and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear, accessible definitions for biomedical terms and concepts used in materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain-language explanations and link to authoritative NIH resources when necessary to ensure audience comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release coordination with funding IC
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information officers must contact the funding NIH institute or center (IC) prior to issuing a press release for coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate content, timing, and any required acknowledgments with the relevant IC(s) before publication; follow internal NIH coordination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required acknowledgments in press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must include specific acknowledgment statements naming the Institute(s)/Center and grant number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgment can appear in the footer or early in the press release; include the precise IC name(s) and the grant number(s) supporting the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclaimer text
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the mandated NIH disclaimer in specified materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the required statement exactly: "The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health." Place in footer or early in the release per NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not for scientific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: This style guide does not apply to scientific publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific manuscripts should follow publication-specific standards such as the American Medical Association (AMA) or National Library of Medicine (NLM) styles instead of this guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and legal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow plain language principles and legal requirements such as the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make content accessible and understandable to lay audiences; adhere to federal plain-language obligations and NIH plain-language resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish-language and multilingual guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the NIH Spanish Style Guide and other NIH-language resources for Spanish-language materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH Spanish guidance for translation choices, regional variants, and culturally appropriate phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility standards (Section 508)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure materials meet Section 508 accessibility standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design web and electronic materials to be accessible (alt text, headings, contrast, transcripts/captions) per Section 508 and NIH accessibility policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PubMed/PubMed Central guidance for citation formats where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For references and links to the scientific literature, use NIH-recommended citation resources and formats consistent with intended audience and medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science and health communication best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply established best practices in science and health communication for clarity, accuracy, and audience engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate evidence-based communication strategies (audience testing, clear calls-to-action, appropriate use of risk/context) and consult NIH communication resources as needed.
